body: Across the cases, the early signal was almost never secret information. It was **publicly visible data that most investors dismissed** because it sat inside a declining or boring narrative. Examples: segment revenue (NVIDIA data center), mix shift (Radico's Prestige & Above share), a new CEO's product reset (Royal Enfield), a policy document (defence indigenisation, PLI), or a capex for import substitution (Deepak phenol). The skill is to follow the second-order effect to where the market has not yet priced it.

`insight:short-seller-reports-outcomes` | 2026-11-19 | tickers: - | confidence: verified

Case outcomes: confirmed frauds -- Luckin (Muddy Waters, admitted within ~2 months), Nikola (Hindenburg, founder convicted), Wirecard (FT/Zatarra/shorts, 5 years early; regulator attacked the shorts), Valeant (Citron, -90%), Enron (Chanos), Lehman (Einhorn). Contested -- Adani (Hindenburg 2023: -60% to -70% drawdowns, partial recovery, SEBI Sep 2025 closed RPT allegations without penalty; other matters pending; Hindenburg closed Jan 2025). Practical rules: (1) Evaluate the evidence type -- primary documents, store counts, registries and ex-employee testimony (Luckin, Nikola) are stronger than valuation arguments; (2) Management response quality: point-by-point rebuttal with documents vs attacks on the messenger (Wirecard, Valeant called reports 'manipulation'); (3) Independent auditor/special audit outcome (KPMG at Wirecard could not verify); (4) Even when not fraud, fragile balance sheets and stretched valuations produce big drawdowns (Adani); (5) Regulators defending a 'national champion' is not evidence. Base rates: academic studies of activist short reports generally find large negative announcement returns that persist on average (exact magnitudes vary; unverified here). For a long-only holder: on a credible report, cut to a size you can hold through a 60% fall, then wait for independent verification.

`case_study:microsoft-nadella-2014-2025` · tickers US-MSFT · confidence: verified

Satya Nadella became CEO Feb 4 2014; stock closed $36.35 that day; market cap ~$300bn; P/E ~13-15x. 'Mobile first, cloud first': Office on iPad (Mar 2014), abandoned the Nokia phone bet (~$7.6bn write-down 2015) [from memory], open-sourced/partnered (Linux on Azure), shifted Office to Office 365 subscriptions. Target of $20bn commercial cloud run-rate by FY18 (from $6.3bn) was beaten in 2017. Market cap >$2tn by 2021, >$3tn by 2024-25; Fool: >1,160% gain since Feb 2014 (2025). Peak ~$555 mid-2025 [unverified] = ~15x plus dividends. Split [approx, my calc]: EPS FY14 ~$2.63 -> FY25 ~$13.6 (~5x); P/E ~14x -> ~35x (~2.5x). Max drawdown: ~-37% in 2022 ($349 -> ~$213). EARLY SIGNAL visible 2014-15: Azure growing >100% y/y, Office 365 consumer/commercial seat growth, deferred revenue rising, a CEO publicly killing the Windows-first culture — while the stock still priced as a declining PC monopoly. Who caught it: ValueAct Capital (Jeff Ubben) built a ~$2bn stake in 2013 and got a board seat (Mason Morfit, 2014) [from memory, unverified in this pass]. Ended/stalled: AI capex surge (2025-26) raised questions about returns; 2026 status not verified here. LESSON: an insider CEO who reallocates capital away from the legacy cash cow toward a recurring-revenue platform can turn a 'value trap' into a 10x+ via both EPS and multiple.

- **Start → end:** $36.35 (Feb 4 2014) → ~$500-555 (2025) [peak unverified] (~14-15x (+divs))
- **EPS vs rerating:** EPS ~5x, P/E ~2.5x
- **Max drawdown:** -37% (2022)
- **Early signal:** Azure >100% growth; O365 seats; culture reset; low P/E
- **Who caught it:** ValueAct / Jeff Ubben [unverified]
- **Ended/stalled:** not clearly ended; AI-capex scrutiny 2025-26
- **Lesson:** new CEO + recurring revenue pivot = EPS + rerating

body:
`strategy:akre-three-legged-stool` | confidence: **verified** | tags: global, india, process, quality, compounding

Three legs, all required: (1) Business - extraordinary economics, measured by high, durable returns on owners' capital (ROE/ROIC) without heavy leverage; (2) People - skilled, honest management that treats shareholders as partners and has a record of good capital allocation; (3) Reinvestment - the ability to reinvest free cash flow at similar high returns for many years (runway). When a 'compounding machine' is found, the default is to hold; turnover is very low and selling happens when a leg breaks (reinvestment runway ends, management changes behaviour), not on valuation alone. Indian checklist translation: ROCE >20% for 7-10 years, low debt, promoters with clean related-party and pledge history, capex funded internally with incremental ROCE staying high, and a TAM that supports a decade of growth. Risk: paying any price for quality (de-rating), and confusing a cyclical peak ROE for a durable one.

`person:group-dalmia` · flag: **mostly-clean** · confidence: verified · tickers: DALBHARAT, DALMIASUG

Flag: MOSTLY-CLEAN (one long-running quid-pro-quo allegation). Dalmia Bharat (cement; consolidated subsidiaries Dalmia Cement (Bharat) and earlier OCL India) and Dalmia Bharat Sugar. Listed-company record: periodic simplification (2018-19 merger of Odisha Cement and the holdco into Dalmia Bharat), buybacks/dividends, no promoter pledging; aggressive capacity expansion via IBC bids (lost Jaiprakash Associates to Adani, 2025-26; acquired Murli Industries and parts of Binani). Allegation: the 2011 CBI case in the Y.S. Jagan Mohan Reddy disproportionate-assets matter alleges Dalmia Cement invested ~Rs 95 cr in Bharathi Cement in return for limestone leases from the Andhra Pradesh government; ED provisionally attached Reddy's shares (~Rs 27.5 cr) and Dalmia Cement land (ED value ~Rs 377 cr; DCBL said ~Rs 793 cr) on 31-Mar-2025; the PMLA Appellate Tribunal partly allowed DCBL's appeal, cutting attributable proceeds of crime from ~Rs 793 cr to ~Rs 92.5 cr; ED reportedly released attached land on 21-Apr-2026 (secondary source). This is an unproven criminal allegation 15 years old; no conviction. Older Dalmia family history (Ramkrishna Dalmia's 1950s conviction; the separate Sanjay Dalmia/GHCL and Vishnu Hari Dalmia branches) should not be conflated with this group. Investor read: operating governance acceptable; political-licensing risk in mining-heavy businesses.

- **allegations:** CBI 2011 / ED 2025 Jagan Reddy quid-pro-quo (pending; proceeds reduced by tribunal)
- **good conduct:** structure simplification; no pledges

body:
`insight:marks-limits-to-negativism-2008` | confidence: verified | date: 2008-10-15

Memos of 19 Sep 2008 and 15 Oct 2008, written in the Lehman panic. Binary framing: 'I think the outlook has to be viewed as binary: will the world end or won't it? If you can't say yes, you have to say no and act accordingly' - if the world ends, nothing you did matters; if it doesn't and you didn't invest, 'we wouldn't have done our job.' Oaktree invested ~$400m a week from 18 Sep 2008 to year-end (~$6bn in distressed debt, $7.5bn firm-wide), buying senior debt at prices that would work even if companies were worth 'only one-quarter or one-third of what the buyout funds had just paid.' The CIO meeting where no scenario was 'too bad' convinced him 'little optimism was embodied in the prices.' Key lines: 'Skepticism and pessimism aren't synonymous. Skepticism calls for pessimism when optimism is excessive. But it also calls for optimism when pessimism is excessive'; in the third stage of a bear market 'everyone agrees things can only get worse', and 'the greater long-term risk probably lies in not investing.' Outcome (per Marks): S&P 500 fell to 735 in Feb 2009, -53% from its 2007 high of 1,549, then recovered. Actionable for India: in a crash, ask whether the system survives; if yes, buy senior/high-quality claims at prices that work in bad cases (2008, Mar-2020 analogues).

Sources:
- https://www.oaktreecapital.com/docs/default-source/memos/2008-10-15-the-limits-to-negativism.pdf
- https://www.oaktreecapital.com/insights/memo/taking-the-temperature
